steps.text: Preheat an oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Line an 11-17-inch baking sheet with aluminum foil and lightly spray with cooking spray.
Mix milk and ranch dressing in a shallow bowl. Place flour in a separate shallow bowl; set aside.
Whisk together bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, seasoned salt, black pepper, celery salt, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, parsley, and basil in a bowl.
Spray bread crumb mixture with cooking spray until damp, then whisk bread crumbs. Repeat spraying and whisking 3 more times to lightly moisten crumb mixture with cooking spray.
Transfer crumb mixture to a large resealable plastic bag.
Gently press tilapia fillets into the flour to coat, and shake off the excess flour.
Dip the fillets into the ranch dressing mixture.
Place all the fillets into the resealable plastic bag; seal bag and shake to coat fish with bread crumb mixture.
Arrange tilapia on prepared baking sheet. Lightly spray the breaded fish with cooking spray.
Bake in the preheated oven until the fish is easily flaked with a fork, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Parmesan Tilapia
raw_recipe.description: Ranch dressing adds a zippy flavor to this crispy baked fish dinner.

review.reviewBody:
Turned out GREAT.... 
I used olive oil instead of cooking spray!!

The BEST! My husband, my 3.5 year old, and I gobbled this up. I used olive oil instead of cooking spray. And I omitted the celery salt (don't have any). I have been using allrecipes.com for years and this is the first recipe that prompted me to rate and review!
Great flavor w/crunchy breading. Loved it! My fish was done at about 16 min. Thanks!!

Very good recipe. I read through the reviews before baking. I also placed mine on a cookie cooling rack on top of a cookie sheet to bake. Worked great! Both sides got nice and crisp! Added a little extra paprika, and left off the basil because I didn't have any. It was very good. Will probably make again.

To the "reviewers" who complain about tilapia based not on this recipe but on it's diet, let me give you some other garbage eaters to avoid - catfish, shrimp, all the bivalves, abalone... getting the idea? Anyway, on to the recipe. I drizzled olive oil into the crumb coating and let the fish rest for about 15 minutes to make sure the crumbs would adhere during baking (I always do this, it really helps!). Wonderful!

This dish was very easy to make and delicious! I didn't have ranch dressing or celery seasoning so I omitted those two ingredients and the fish was still very flavorful. 

I will definitely make this again!

Five stars once you edit recipe for sure. Totally skip the oil and the spray, also the bag. No need for them! Use non-stick aluminum foil in your pan. I prepared the ranch/milk bowl, flour in another, and breadcrumb mixture in third bowl. (I always use smoked paprika for extra flavor.) I dredged filets in flour, then ranch, then into breadcrumbs, placed on foil lined baking dish & into the oven. I flipped about half way, and they were perfectly browned on both sides. Delish!

I don't care for fish, so I made this for my boyfriend and his son. Because of their reaction, I eventually took a bite to see what all the fuss was about. This is good, according to me. According to them, it is outrageously delicious! They absolutely loved it, and not a bit was leftover! I used my homemade seasoned breadcrumbs, but still went ahead a seasoned as the recipe states. Like other reviewers, I used olive oil to moisten the crumbs. Instead of laying the fish on the foil lined baking sheet, I lightly sprayed a cooling rack with Pam, placed that on the baking sheet, and put the fish on the rack. This resulted in crispy fish on both sides, and also allowed the fish to be easily moved to a plate without leaving any of the coating behind. I served this with a dollop of goat cheese and herb ice cream, for dipping. It was a huge success. Thanks for a great and easy recipe Mike :)

Came out very good and was crispy. I did not have any ranch so I used an egg with the milk and lemon and put the dill as well cilantro and chili powder in the breading mixmix. I am on a low sodium diet so I omitted the salt and used celery powder instead of salt, and also used No salt (a salt substitute) I double coated the fish and baked as directed. I was afraid the temperature was too high but it worked just right, and all the breading stayed on the fish. Served with tartar sauce and corn, it was very good.

Added lemon pepper since hubby LOVES it. Also a big thanks for the suggestion to put fish on cookie cooling rack while baking! They turned out crispy all over!!! Never would have thought of that! AWESOME!!!!!

This sounded good but unnecessarily labor intensive.I gave it t 5 stars with these simplifying steps: Heat oven to 350. Line baking sheet with foil. Place tilapia on a plate. Spread with bottled ranch dressing, salt to taste. Sprinkle Italian seasoned bread crumbs over fish. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top of that. Spritz with olive oil. Lay fish crumb side down on foil. Repeat process to cover tops of fish with ranch, breadcrumbs, cheese & spritzed olive oil. Bake at 350 for 30 mins. Yum!

I didn't have onion powder so I used onion while baking. I didn't do the plastic bag method. After dipping in Ranch mix I pressed in a bowl of the dry bread crumb mix. I did not spray the bread crumbs with cooking spray. I don't like cooking spray. After Bread crumbs I put them in a backing dish with olive oil and onions. I sprayed the fish filets in the baking dish with olive oil. Next time I will cut the Celery Salt. Was very good and I liked it. Good recipe.
This was delicious! Everyone from age 45 to 16! It was a hit with everyone tonight! I substituted melted, salted butter for the cooking spray, my only alteration.
Meh. The 4 year old, who isn't crazy about fish, loved it! I only had enough crumbs for on top which was much easier to assemble.
This was delicious! As others suggested used olive oil versus spraying the bread crumbs. Also, dubbed bottled Caesar dressing for the Ranch since that’s what I had. Will make again.
Definitely a hit with my family!!
I used cod filets instead of Talapia. Delicious.
